newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian banking system's Q1 net up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Colombian banking system's Q1 net up sharply.

text.p: BOGOTA, May 7 Reuter - Colombia's banking and financial system saw its net profits rise 49 percent in the first quarter of 1997 over the same period last year to a total of 235.3 billion pesos, the Banking Superintendency said Wednesday.
It gave no comparative figure for the first quarter of 1996 but said total assets, as of March 31, were up 23 percent over the year-ago period at 60 trillion pesos.
The superintendency, a state-run regulatory body, said 53 percent of Colombia's banks and financial institutions were in conditions that could be described as "highly solvent."

Past-due loans fell to 47 percent of total loan portfolios from 54 percent in the first quarter of last year, according to the superintendency, which noted that overall demand for credit had dropped proportionately.
